_comment: Hand-written additions per registry id, merged by gen_reference.py. Keys: 'note' (HTML, appended to the description), 'perm' (name of the Project Settings permission the row needs, see EngineApi.cpp perm::allowed), 'script_sig' / 'script_returns' (the Lua/Python call when it differs from the registry signature), 'examples' ({lua, python} source, rendered with the language switcher). Steps 3-8 of Thema 79 fill this per group.

log.note: Lua also accepts a number; Python only a str.

examples.lua:
local M = {}

-- True when target lies within coneDeg degrees around the direction
-- (fx, fy, fz) this entity faces.
function M.canSee(self, target, fx, fy, fz, coneDeg)
    local x, y, z = horizon.getPosition(self.entityId)
    local tx, ty, tz = horizon.getPosition(target)
    local dx, dy, dz = horizon.math.normalize3(tx - x, ty - y, tz - z)
    local limit = horizon.math.cos(horizon.math.radians(coneDeg / 2))
    return horizon.math.dot3(dx, dy, dz, fx, fy, fz) >= limit
end

return M
examples.python:
import horizon

class ViewCone(horizon.Behavior):
    def can_see(self, target, fx, fy, fz, cone_deg):
        """True when target lies within cone_deg degrees around (fx, fy, fz)."""
        x, y, z = horizon.getPosition(self.entity_id)
        tx, ty, tz = horizon.getPosition(target)
        dx, dy, dz = horizon.math.normalize3(tx - x, ty - y, tz - z)
        limit = horizon.math.cos(horizon.math.radians(cone_deg / 2))
        return horizon.math.dot3(dx, dy, dz, fx, fy, fz) >= limit

string.find.note: In Lua, add 1 before handing the result to string.sub.

examples.lua:
local M = {}

-- "volume = 75" -> "volume", 75. Positions count from 0.
local function parse(line)
    local eq = horizon.string.find(line, "=")
    if eq < 0 then return nil end
    local key = horizon.string.trim(horizon.string.substring(line, 0, eq))
    local rest = horizon.string.substring(line, eq + 1, horizon.string.length(line))
    return key, horizon.string.toNumber(rest)
end

function M.onStart(self)
    local key, value = parse("volume = 75")
    if key then horizon.log(key .. " is " .. value) end
end

return M

local M = {}

function M.onStart(self)
    -- Without this, every launch rolls the same numbers. Seed in one
    -- script only: every seed restarts the sequence for all of them.
    horizon.random.seed(os.time())
end

function M.roll(self)
    local eyes = horizon.random.rangeInt(1, 6)      -- 1 to 6, both included
    local critical = horizon.random.chance(0.05)     -- one in twenty
    return eyes, critical
end

return M
examples.python:
import time
import horizon

class Dice(horizon.Behavior):
    def on_start(self):
        # Without this, every launch rolls the same numbers. Seed in one
        # script only: every seed restarts the sequence for all of them.
        horizon.random.seed(int(time.time()))

    def roll(self):
        eyes = horizon.random.rangeInt(1, 6)     # 1 to 6, both included
        critical = horizon.random.chance(0.05)   # one in twenty
        return eyes, critical

time.pause.note: Input actions stop arriving unless they have Fires while the game is paused ticked.

examples.lua:
local M = {}

-- "Pause" is an input action with "Fires while the game is paused"
-- ticked; without it the second press would never arrive.
function M.onInputPressed(self, name)
    if name ~= "Pause" then return end
    if horizon.time.isPaused() then
        horizon.time.resume()
    else
        horizon.time.pause()
    end
end

function M.onCollisionEnter(self, other)
    horizon.time.hitStop(0.1)   -- a landed hit freezes for a tenth of a second
end

return M

time.hitStop.note: 0 or less does nothing, and does not end a hit stop that is running.

timer.after.note: 0 also when 64 timers are already running.

timer.every.note: 0 when the interval is under 0.001 seconds or 64 timers are already running.

examples.lua:
local M = {}

function M.onStart(self)
    self.autosave = horizon.timer.every(30)
    self.hint = horizon.timer.after(5)
end

function M.onTimer(self, handle)
    if handle == self.autosave then
        horizon.log("autosave")
    elseif handle == self.hint then
        horizon.log("Press E to open the door")
    end
    -- any other handle belongs to another script
end

return M

timer.cancelAll.note: That includes the timers of every other script and of the GameInstance.

datetime.now.note: Accurate only to about a minute, see the known issue.

examples.lua:
local M = {}

local DAYS = { [0] = "Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday",
               "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday" }

function M.onStart(self)
    local now = horizon.datetime.now()
    horizon.log("Today is " .. DAYS[horizon.datetime.weekday(now)] .. ", "
                .. horizon.datetime.format(now, "%d.%m.%Y"))
    -- To the second: from Lua itself until the precision issue is fixed.
    horizon.log("It is " .. os.date("%H:%M:%S"))
end

return M
examples.python:
import time
import horizon

DAYS = ["Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday",
        "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday"]

class ClockLabel(horizon.Behavior):
    def on_start(self):
        now = horizon.datetime.now()
        day = DAYS[horizon.datetime.weekday(now)]
        horizon.log(f"Today is {day}, {horizon.datetime.format(now, '%d.%m.%Y')}")
        # To the second: from Python itself until the precision issue is fixed.
        horizon.log("It is " + time.strftime("%H:%M:%S"))

entity.spawn.note: An empty name becomes "Entity"; parent 0 puts it at the top level. Known issue: the entity gets no transform, so position calls on it do nothing (see the group notes).

entity.self.note: Always 0 in Lua and Python; use self.entityId / self.entity_id.

entity.distance.note: An entity without a transform counts as standing at the origin.

examples.lua:
local M = {}

-- Opens the gate once the boss is gone. Look the ids up once, not every
-- frame: findByName walks every named entity.
function M.onStart(self)
    self.boss = horizon.entity.findByName("Boss")
    self.gate = horizon.entity.findByName("Gate")
end

function M.onUpdate(self, dt)
    if self.gate ~= 0 and not horizon.entity.exists(self.boss) then
        horizon.entity.destroy(self.gate)   -- takes its children along
        self.gate = 0
    end
end

return M

entity.saveState.note: Needs play mode, an active save and an enabled Save State component; see the group notes.

entity.applySavedState.note: On an entity with a physics body it moves the body too and stops its motion.

scene.load.note: In the editor's play mode this only logs a warning.

scene.activate.note: Logs a warning when nothing was preloaded. In the editor's play mode this only logs a warning.

scene.loadAdditive.note: Known issue: the position pin is typed as a colour, so Lua and Python must pass four numbers; the fourth is ignored. With three, Lua raises bad argument #6 and Python IndexError. An offset of 0, 0, 0 leaves the zone where its scene put it.

examples.lua:
local M = {}

-- This entity is a trigger volume at the start of the corridor. The cave
-- loads hidden, 200 m along X, while the player walks; the door shows it.
function M.onBeginOverlap(self, other)
    if self.zone then return end
    -- The position takes FOUR numbers from a script; the fourth is ignored.
    self.zone = horizon.scene.loadAdditive("Scenes/Cave.hescene", true, 200, 0, 0, 0)
end

-- "Interact" is an input action.
function M.onInputPressed(self, name)
    if name == "Interact" and self.zone then
        horizon.scene.showZone(self.zone)   -- queued behind the load
    end
end

return M

scene.zonePosition.note: 0, 0, 0 until the zone has arrived, the frame after loadAdditive.

scene.zoneScene.note: Empty until the zone has arrived.

scene.setZonePosition.note: Rebuilds the zone's collision at the new place, which stops moving bodies in it.

save.create.note: Replaces the active save without writing it.

save.setNumber.note: An Int or Enum field drops the fraction toward zero.

save.getNumber.note: A Float field keeps about seven digits.

save.setStruct.note: Needs a value from horizon.structs.<Name>() or getStruct; a table without __type is refused.

save.delete.note: Deleting the active save leaves it active; write would create the file again.

examples.lua:
local M = {}
local SLOT = "slot1"

-- "level" (Int) and "stats" (a struct with "kills") are fields of the
-- project's SaveGame Template.
function M.onStart(self)
    -- Continue from the save if there is one, else start a new one.
    if not (horizon.save.exists(SLOT) and horizon.save.load(SLOT)) then
        horizon.save.create(SLOT)
    end
    horizon.log(string.format("Level %d", horizon.save.getNumber("level", 1)))
end

-- This entity is the checkpoint's trigger volume.
function M.onBeginOverlap(self, other)
    horizon.save.setNumber("level", horizon.save.getNumber("level", 1) + 1)
    local stats = horizon.save.getStruct("stats")   -- keeps __type
    stats.kills = stats.kills + 1
    horizon.save.setStruct("stats", stats)
    horizon.save.write()   -- nothing is on disk before this
end

return M
examples.python:
import horizon

SLOT = "slot1"

class Checkpoint(horizon.Behavior):
    # "level" (Int) and "stats" (a struct with "kills") are fields of the
    # project's SaveGame Template.
    def on_start(self):
        # Continue from the save if there is one, else start a new one.
        if not (horizon.save.exists(SLOT) and horizon.save.load(SLOT)):
            horizon.save.create(SLOT)
        horizon.log(f"Level {horizon.save.getNumber('level', 1):.0f}")

    # This entity is the checkpoint's trigger volume.
    def on_begin_overlap(self, other):
        horizon.save.setNumber("level", horizon.save.getNumber("level", 1) + 1)
        stats = horizon.save.getStruct("stats")   # keeps __type
        stats["kills"] += 1
        horizon.save.setStruct("stats", stats)
        horizon.save.write()   # nothing is on disk before this

examples.lua:
local M = {}
local FILE = "settings.json"

-- settings.json in the game's data folder, e.g.
-- {"video": {"width": 1920}, "profiles": [{"name": "Ada"}, {"name": "Lin"}]}
function M.onStart(self)
    local doc = horizon.fs.readText(FILE)   -- "" when the file is missing
    local width = horizon.json.getNumber(doc, "video.width", 1280)
    for i = 0, horizon.json.count(doc, "profiles") - 1 do
        horizon.log(horizon.json.getString(doc, "profiles[" .. i .. "].name", "?"))
    end
    -- Setters return the new text; store it and write it back yourself.
    doc = horizon.json.setNumber(doc, "video.width", width)
    doc = horizon.json.setBool(doc, "video.seen", true)
    horizon.fs.writeText(FILE, doc)
end

return M
examples.python:
import horizon

FILE = "settings.json"

class SettingsFile(horizon.Behavior):
    # settings.json in the game's data folder, e.g.
    # {"video": {"width": 1920}, "profiles": [{"name": "Ada"}, {"name": "Lin"}]}
    def on_start(self):
        doc = horizon.fs.readText(FILE)   # "" when the file is missing
        width = horizon.json.getNumber(doc, "video.width", 1280)
        for i in range(horizon.json.count(doc, "profiles")):
            horizon.log(horizon.json.getString(doc, f"profiles[{i}].name", "?"))
        # Setters return the new text; store it and write it back yourself.
        doc = horizon.json.setNumber(doc, "video.width", width)
        doc = horizon.json.setBool(doc, "video.seen", True)
        horizon.fs.writeText(FILE, doc)

json.getNumber.note: Exact for whole numbers up to 16 777 216.

json.has.note: true also for a key whose value is null.

json.setNumber.note: Writes whole numbers as 3.0 and keeps about seven digits.
